input.command: python3 -c "import reportlab; print('reportlab', reportlab.Version)" 2>&1; python3 -c "import fpdf; print('fpdf ok')" 2>&1; mkdir -p /mnt/session/outputs && ls -la /mnt/session/outputs

cd /mnt/session/outputs && python3 -c "
from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import letter
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas
c = canvas.Canvas('nimbus_test.pdf', pagesize=letter)
c.setTitle('Nimbus test')
c.setFont('Helvetica-Bold', 24)
c.drawString(72, 700, 'Nimbus test')
c.setFont('Helvetica', 14)
c.drawString(72, 660, 'Hello from the sandbox.')
c.showPage()
c.save()
" && ls -la nimbus_test.pdf && python3 -c "
import re;d=open('nimbus_test.pdf','rb').read();print('pages:',len(re.findall(rb'/Type\s*/Page[^s]',d)))"; which pdftotext && pdftotext nimbus_test.pdf -

content.text:
I made the one-page PDF with reportlab and saved it at `/mnt/session/outputs/nimbus_test.pdf`.

It is titled "Nimbus test" and contains the line "Hello from the sandbox." I checked that it has one page and that the text extracts correctly.

The title is also set as the PDF's document title. I added it as a large heading above the line, so the page shows "Nimbus test" and then the sentence. If you want only the sentence on the page, I can remove the heading.
